title: Investigation of Spacetime and Its Adequate Coordinate System with Observations by Spacelab and Artemis II
content:
The International Astronomical Union (IAU) realized, that General Relativity Theory (GRT) with its hypothetic coordinate systems is insufficient for space flight.
The IAU proclaimed the problem of finding an Adequate Coordinate System (ACS).
As a provisional solution, the IAU recommended Celestial Reference Systems (CRS).
It has been shown that there is an ACS at each point in the universe, and near a celestial body, the ACS is at rest at the celestial body's field.
In the Artemis II mission, the spacecraft traveled through a region, in which a superposition of moving fields takes place, originating from Earth, Sun and Moon.
Present - day advanced theories about GRT,  such as the PPN and PNA,
treat only a single CRS in each region.
According the superposition problem of moving fields is identified.
A deep solution about the physics of space and time is used,
in order to solve this problem.
The solution is applied to the Artemis II mission.
